class matcha.sklearn.Ensemble(model: matcha.sklearn.base_sklearn_model.BaseScikitLearnModel, n_models: int = 5, seed: int = 0)[source]

Ensemble of sklearn-API models trained via cross-validation.

The ensemble is constructed from a template model instance (any concrete BaseScikitLearnModel subclass such as GINRegressor). The template is deep-copied n_models times, each copy receiving a different random seed.

Example usage:

from matcha.sklearn import GINRegressor, Ensemble

model = GINRegressor(num_epochs=50, enc_num_layers=3)
ensemble = Ensemble(model=model, n_models=5)
ensemble.fit(train_mols, train_y)
mean, std = ensemble.predict(test_mols)
params
property calibrator

The ensemble-level calibration object, or None.

property explainer

The explainability object from the first ensemble member, or None.

property model_box

List of individual model members in the ensemble.

property cv_idx

Cross-validation split indices used during fitting, or None.

property is_classifier: bool

Whether the ensemble members are classifiers.

property task_type: str

‘binary_classification’ or ‘regression’.

Type:

transform(x: list[rdkit.Chem.rdchem.Mol], y: numpy.ndarray = None, bound_mask: list[str] | None = None, is_training: bool = True)[source]

Transform molecules into the featurized dataset format.

Delegates to the first ensemble member’s transform. Fitting of scalers is deferred to the per-member CV loop inside fit().

Parameters:

  • x (list[Mol]) – list of RDKit molecules to featurize

  • y (np.ndarray) – property labels (optional)

  • bound_mask (list[str] | None) – censor information on labels

  • is_training (bool) – whether to fit standardizers (kept for API consistency)

Returns:

featurized dataset

Return type:

StackDataset

class matcha.sklearn.RoFormerClassifier(enc_hidden_dim: int = 256, enc_expansion_dim: int = 1024, enc_num_heads: int = 8, enc_num_layers: int = 3, enc_attention_dropout: float = 0.1, enc_hidden_dropout: float = 0.1, pred_hidden_dims: list[int] = [256, 256], pred_task_head_dims: list[int] | None = None, pred_activation: str = 'gelu', pred_dropout: float = 0.2, num_endpoints: int = 1, loss_fn: str = 'bce', loss_args: dict = {}, optimizer: str = 'adamw', optimizer_args: dict = {'lr': 0.0001, 'weight_decay': 0.0001}, scheduler: str = 'warmup_linear_decay', scheduler_args: dict = {'min_lr': 1e-05}, num_epochs: int = 100, batch_size: int = 64, stochastic_weight_averaging: bool = False, early_stopping: bool = True, patience: int = 10, devices: int = 1, accelerator: str = 'gpu', max_length: int = 200, num_augmentations: int = 7, feature_list: list[str] | None = None, label_encoder_params: dict = {}, label_transform_map: str | list[str] | dict | None = None, augment_resonance: bool = False, seed: int = 0)[source]

Bases: matcha.sklearn.clm.base_sklearn_clm.BaseScikitLearnCLM, matcha.sklearn.base_sklearn_model.ScikitLearnClassifierMixin

Chemical language transformer using the RoFormer architecture for classification.

Uses rotary position embeddings (RoPE) within a BERT-style transformer encoder to learn contextual token representations from SMILES strings. Only compatible with classification datasets. Inherits from BaseScikitLearnCLM.

References:

  • Devlin et al., BERT (2019): https://arxiv.org/abs/1810.04805

  • Su et al., RoFormer (2021): https://arxiv.org/abs/2106.09553

Example usage:

model = RoFormerClassifier()
model.fit(train_mols, train_y)
predictions = model.predict(test_mols)
Parameters:

  • enc_hidden_dim (int) – token embedding dimensionality, defaults to 256

  • enc_expansion_dim (int) – feed-forward expansion dimensionality inside transformer blocks, defaults to 1024

  • enc_num_heads (int) – number of attention heads, defaults to 8

  • enc_num_layers (int) – number of transformer blocks, defaults to 3

  • enc_attention_dropout (float) – dropout for attention weights, defaults to 0.1

  • enc_hidden_dropout (float) – dropout in dense layers inside transformer blocks, defaults to 0.1

  • pred_hidden_dims (list[int]) – shape of hidden MLP layers in the predictor, defaults to [256, 256]

  • pred_task_head_dims (list[int] | None) – shape of the MLP layers dedicated to each task independently, defaults to None

  • pred_activation (str) – activation function in the predictor, defaults to ‘gelu’

  • pred_dropout (float) – dropout rate in the predictor, defaults to 0.2

  • num_endpoints (int) – number of endpoints (if multitasking) or classes (if classification) to predict, defaults to 1

  • loss_fn (str) – loss function to optimize, defaults to ‘bce’

  • loss_args (dict) – additional arguments for the loss function, defaults to {}

  • optimizer (str) – optimizer to use while training, defaults to ‘adamw’

  • optimizer_args (dict) – additional arguments for the optimizer, defaults to {‘lr’: 1e-4, ‘weight_decay’: 1e-4}

  • scheduler (str) – learning rate scheduler, defaults to ‘warmup_linear_decay’

  • scheduler_args (dict) – additional arguments for the scheduler, defaults to {‘min_lr’: 1e-5}. If ‘total_steps’ is not provided, it is auto-computed as num_epochs * ceil(len(train_data) / batch_size).

  • num_epochs (int) – number of epochs to train for, defaults to 100

  • batch_size (int) – batch size for training and prediction, defaults to 64

  • stochastic_weight_averaging (bool) – whether to add SWA epochs after regular training, defaults to False

  • early_stopping (bool) – whether to use early stopping, defaults to True

  • patience (int) – how many epochs to wait before early stopping, defaults to 10

  • devices (int) – number of devices for training, defaults to 1

  • accelerator (str) – hardware accelerator (‘cpu’, ‘gpu’, ‘tpu’, or ‘hpu’), defaults to ‘gpu’

  • max_length (int) – maximum SMILES length allowed, defaults to 200

  • num_augmentations (int) – number of SMILES augmentations for training, defaults to 7

  • feature_list (list[str] | None) – list of additional descriptor sets to compute, defaults to None

  • label_encoder_params (dict) – parameters for the label encoder, defaults to {}

  • label_transform_map (str | list[str] | dict | None) – label transform configuration, defaults to None

  • augment_resonance (bool) – whether to augment with resonance structures, defaults to False

  • seed (int) – random seed for reproducibility, defaults to 0

class matcha.sklearn.CNNClassifier(enc_hidden_dim: int = 256, enc_kernel_dims: list[int] = [3, 5, 8, 11, 14], enc_num_heads: int = 8, enc_activation: str = 'swish', enc_dropout: float = 0.2, pred_hidden_dims: list[int] = [256, 256], pred_task_head_dims: list[int] | None = None, pred_activation: str = 'swish', pred_dropout: float = 0.2, num_endpoints: int = 1, loss_fn: str = 'bce', loss_args: dict = {}, optimizer: str = 'adamw', optimizer_args: dict = {'lr': 0.0001, 'weight_decay': 0.0001}, scheduler: str = 'warmup_linear_decay', scheduler_args: dict = {'min_lr': 1e-05}, num_epochs: int = 100, batch_size: int = 64, stochastic_weight_averaging: bool = False, early_stopping: bool = True, patience: int = 10, devices: int = 1, accelerator: str = 'gpu', max_length: int = 200, num_augmentations: int = 7, feature_list: list[str] | None = None, label_encoder_params: dict = {}, label_transform_map: str | list[str] | dict | None = None, augment_resonance: bool = False, seed: int = 0)[source]

Bases: matcha.sklearn.clm.base_sklearn_clm.BaseScikitLearnCLM, matcha.sklearn.base_sklearn_model.ScikitLearnClassifierMixin

1D convolutional neural network (CNN) for molecular property classification.

Learns to embed chemical language (e.g. SMILES) via convolutional layers and predict properties in an end-to-end manner. Only compatible with classification datasets. Inherits from BaseScikitLearnCLM.

References:

  • Boldini et al., J. Cheminform. (2024): https://arxiv.org/abs/2407.12152

  • Boldini et al., Digital Discovery (2023): https://pubs.rsc.org/en/content/articlehtml/2023/dd/d2dd00099g

Example usage:

model = CNNClassifier()
model.fit(train_mols, train_y)
predictions = model.predict(test_mols)
Parameters:

  • enc_hidden_dim (int) – number of filters per convolutional layer, defaults to 256

  • enc_kernel_dims (list[int]) – kernel sizes for each convolutional layer, defaults to [3, 5, 8, 11, 14]

  • enc_num_heads (int) – number of attention heads for computing self-attention, defaults to 8

  • enc_activation (str) – activation function to use throughout the encoder, defaults to ‘swish’

  • enc_dropout (float) – dropout rate across the encoder, defaults to 0.2

  • pred_hidden_dims (list[int]) – shape of hidden MLP layers in the predictor, defaults to [256, 256]

  • pred_task_head_dims (list[int] | None) – shape of the MLP layers dedicated to each task independently, defaults to None

  • pred_activation (str) – activation function to use in the predictor, defaults to ‘swish’

  • pred_dropout (float) – dropout rate across the predictor, defaults to 0.2

  • num_endpoints (int) – number of endpoints (if multitasking) or classes (if classification) to predict, defaults to 1

  • loss_fn (str) – loss function to optimize, defaults to ‘bce’

  • loss_args (dict) – additional arguments for the loss function, defaults to {}

  • optimizer (str) – optimizer to use while training, defaults to ‘adamw’

  • optimizer_args (dict) – additional arguments for the optimizer, defaults to {‘lr’: 1e-4, ‘weight_decay’: 1e-4}

AttentiveFP graph attention classifier.

Uses a graph attention mechanism for molecular representation learning and property prediction, as described in Pushing the Boundaries of Molecular Representation for Drug Discovery with the Graph Attention Mechanism. Compatible with classification datasets only.

Inherits from BaseScikitLearnGNN for graph-specific datamodule creation and collate-aware dataloading.

References:

  • Xiong et al., Pushing the Boundaries of Molecular Representation for Drug Discovery with the Graph Attention Mechanism https://doi.org/10.1021/acs.jmedchem.9b00959

Example usage:

model = AttentiveFPClassifier()
model.fit(train_mols, train_y)
predictions = model.predict(test_mols)
Parameters:

  • enc_num_layers (int) – number of encoder layers for message passing, defaults to 2

  • enc_atom_hidden_dim (int) – encoder output atom feature dimensionality, defaults to 256

  • enc_jk (str) – encoder jumping knowledge strategy, defaults to ‘last’

  • enc_readout (str) – encoder aggregation for molecule-level embeddings, defaults to ‘virtualnode’

  • enc_dropout (float) – dropout rate across the encoder, defaults to 0.2

  • pred_hidden_dims (list[int]) – shape of hidden MLP layers in the predictor, defaults to [256, 256]

  • pred_activation (str) – activation function in the predictor, defaults to ‘swish’

  • optimizer_args (dict) – optimizer arguments, defaults to {‘lr’: 1e-4, ‘weight_decay’: 1e-4}

  • scheduler (str) – learning rate scheduler, defaults to ‘warmup_linear_decay’

  • scheduler_args (dict) – scheduler arguments, defaults to {‘min_lr’: 1e-5}

  • num_epochs (int) – number of training epochs, defaults to 100

  • batch_size (int) – batch size for training and prediction, defaults to 64

  • stochastic_weight_averaging (bool) – whether to use SWA, defaults to False

Graph Isomorphism Network (GIN) classifier.

Learns to embed molecular graphs and predict properties in an end-to-end manner using message-passing with injective aggregation. Compatible with classification datasets only.

Inherits from BaseScikitLearnGNN for graph-specific datamodule creation and collate-aware dataloading.

References:

  • Xu et al., How Powerful are Graph Neural Networks? https://arxiv.org/abs/1810.00826

Example usage:

model = GINClassifier()
model.fit(train_mols, train_y)
predictions = model.predict(test_mols)
Parameters:

  • enc_num_layers (int) – number of encoder layers for message passing, defaults to 3

  • enc_atom_hidden_dim (int) – encoder output atom feature dimensionality, defaults to 256

  • enc_aggregation (str) – encoder aggregation strategy for message passing, defaults to ‘VariancePreservingAggregation’

  • enc_jk (str) – encoder jumping knowledge strategy, defaults to ‘last’

  • enc_norm (str | None) – which norm to use inside GIN layers in the encoder, defaults to ‘batch’

  • enc_readout (str) – encoder aggregation strategy for returning molecule-level embeddings, defaults to ‘vpa’

  • enc_dropout (float) – dropout rate across the encoder, defaults to 0.2

  • enc_activation (str) – activation function to use across the encoder, defaults to ‘swish’

  • pred_hidden_dims (list[int]) – shape of hidden MLP layers in the predictor, defaults to [256, 256]

  • pred_task_head_dims (list[int] | None) – shape of the MLP layers dedicated to each task independently, defaults to None

  • pred_activation (str) – activation function to use across the predictor, defaults to ‘swish’

  • pred_dropout (float) – dropout rate across the predictor, defaults to 0.2

  • num_endpoints (int) – number of endpoints (if multitasking) or classes (if classification) to predict, defaults to 1

  • loss_fn (str) – loss function to optimize, defaults to ‘bce’

  • loss_args (dict) – additional arguments for the loss function, defaults to {}

  • optimizer (str) – optimizer to use while training, defaults to ‘adamw’

  • optimizer_args (dict) – additional arguments for the optimizer, defaults to {‘lr’: 1e-4, ‘weight_decay’: 1e-4}

  • scheduler (str) – scheduler to change the learning rate during training, defaults to ‘warmup_linear_decay’

  • scheduler_args (dict) – additional arguments for the scheduler, defaults to {‘min_lr’: 1e-5}. If ‘total_steps’ is not provided, it is auto-computed as num_epochs * ceil(len(train_data) / batch_size).

  • num_epochs (int) – number of epochs to train for, defaults to 100

  • batch_size (int) – batch size to use for training and prediction, defaults to 64

  • stochastic_weight_averaging (bool) – whether to add a few epochs with SWA on top of regular training, defaults to False

  • early_stopping (bool) – whether to use early stopping, defaults to True

  • patience (int) – how many epochs to wait before early stopping, defaults to 20

  • devices (int) – how many devices to use for training, defaults to 1

  • accelerator (str) – hardware accelerator to use for training, defaults to ‘gpu’

  • rwse_k (int) – number of random walk structural encoding dimensions, defaults to 0

  • laplacian_k (int) – number of Laplacian positional encoding components, defaults to 0

  • elstatic_k (int) – number of electrostatic encoding dimensions, defaults to 0

  • distmat_k (int) – number of distance matrix encoding dimensions, defaults to 0

  • rrwp_k (int) – number of relative random walk probability dimensions, defaults to 0

  • num_virtual_nodes (int) – number of virtual nodes to add, defaults to 0

  • enc_eps (float) – initial value of the eps term in GINEConv, defaults to 0.0

  • enc_train_eps (bool) – whether to learn eps as a parameter (paper-recommended GIN-ε variant), defaults to True

  • feature_list (list[str] | None) – list of strings defining which molecular feature set to compute, defaults to None

  • label_encoder_params (dict) – additional parameters for the label encoder, defaults to {}

  • label_transform_map (str | list[str] | dict | None) – label transform specification, defaults to None

  • augment_resonance (bool) – whether to augment with resonance structures, defaults to False

  • seed (int) – random seed for reproducibility, defaults to 0

  • pred_activation (str) – activation function to use across the predictor, defaults to ‘swish’

  • pred_dropout (float) – dropout rate across the predictor, defaults to 0.2

  • num_endpoints (int) – number of endpoints to predict, defaults to 1

  • loss_fn (str) – loss function to optimize, defaults to ‘mse’

E(3)-equivariant graph neural network classifier for molecular conformers.

Implements the EGNN architecture from Satorras et al., E(n) Equivariant Graph Neural Networks (arXiv:2102.09844). Learns to embed molecular conformers using equivariant message passing over 3D coordinates and predict properties in an end-to-end manner. Compatible with classification datasets only.

Inherits from BaseScikitLearnGNN3D for common training and predicting routines.

References

  • https://arxiv.org/abs/2102.09844

Example usage:

model = E3GNNClassifier()
model.fit(train_mols, train_y)
predictions = model.predict(test_mols)
Parameters:

  • enc_num_layers (int) – Number of encoder layers for equivariant message passing, defaults to 3.

  • enc_atom_hidden_dim (int) – Encoder atom feature dimensionality, defaults to 128.

  • enc_m_dim (int) – Dimensionality of the message MLP intermediate layer, defaults to 16.

  • enc_fourier_features (int) – Number of Fourier features for distance encoding, defaults to 4.

  • enc_soft_edge (bool) – Whether to apply soft edge weighting, defaults to False.

  • enc_norm_feats (bool) – Whether to normalise node features, defaults to True.

  • enc_norm_coors (bool) – Whether to normalise coordinate updates, defaults to True.

  • enc_update_coors (bool) – Whether to update coordinates during message passing, defaults to True.

  • enc_jk (str) – Jumping knowledge strategy, defaults to ‘last’.

  • enc_readout (str) – Aggregation strategy for molecule-level embeddings, defaults to ‘vpa’.

  • enc_dropout (float) – Encoder dropout rate, defaults to 0.2.

  • enc_activation (str) – Encoder activation function, defaults to ‘swish’.

  • pred_hidden_dims (list[int]) – Hidden layer dimensions in the predictor MLP, defaults to [128, 128].

E(3)-equivariant graph neural network regressor for molecular conformers.

Implements the EGNN architecture from Satorras et al., E(n) Equivariant Graph Neural Networks (arXiv:2102.09844). Learns to embed molecular conformers using equivariant message passing over 3D coordinates and predict continuous properties in an end-to-end manner. Compatible with regression datasets only.

Inherits from BaseScikitLearnGNN3D for common training and predicting routines.

References

  • https://arxiv.org/abs/2102.09844

Example usage:

model = E3GNNRegressor()
model.fit(train_mols, train_y)
predictions = model.predict(test_mols)
Parameters:

  • enc_num_layers (int) – Number of encoder layers for equivariant message passing, defaults to 3.

  • enc_atom_hidden_dim (int) – Encoder atom feature dimensionality, defaults to 128.

  • enc_fourier_features (int) – Number of Fourier features for distance encoding, defaults to 4.

  • enc_soft_edge (bool) – Whether to apply soft edge weighting, defaults to False.

  • enc_norm_feats (bool) – Whether to normalise node features, defaults to True.

  • enc_norm_coors (bool) – Whether to normalise coordinate updates, defaults to True.

  • enc_update_coors (bool) – Whether to update coordinates during message passing, defaults to True.

  • enc_jk (str) – Jumping knowledge strategy, defaults to ‘last’.

  • enc_readout (str) – Aggregation strategy for molecule-level embeddings, defaults to ‘vpa’.

  • enc_dropout (float) – Encoder dropout rate, defaults to 0.2.

  • enc_activation (str) – Encoder activation function, defaults to ‘swish’.

  • pred_hidden_dims (list[int]) – Hidden layer dimensions in the predictor MLP, defaults to [128, 128].

  • pred_task_head_dims (list[int] | None) – Per-task head dimensions, defaults to None.

  • pred_activation (str) – Predictor activation function, defaults to ‘swish’.

  • pred_dropout (float) – Predictor dropout rate, defaults to 0.2.

  • num_endpoints (int) – Number of endpoints to predict, defaults to 1.

  • loss_fn (str) – Loss function, defaults to ‘mse’.

  • loss_args (dict) – Additional loss function arguments, defaults to {}.

  • optimizer (str) – Optimizer, defaults to ‘adamw’.

  • optimizer_args (dict) – Optimizer arguments, defaults to {‘lr’: 1e-4, ‘weight_decay’: 1e-4}.

  • scheduler (str) – Learning rate scheduler, defaults to ‘warmup_cosine_annealing’.

  • scheduler_args (dict) – Scheduler arguments, defaults to {‘min_lr’: 1e-5}. If ‘total_steps’ is not provided, it is auto-computed as num_epochs * ceil(len(train_data) / batch_size).

  • num_epochs (int) – Number of training epochs, defaults to 50.

  • batch_size (int) – Batch size for training and prediction, defaults to 64.

  • stochastic_weight_averaging (bool) – Whether to apply SWA after regular training, defaults to False.

  • early_stopping (bool) – Whether to enable early stopping, defaults to True.

  • patience (int) – Early stopping patience in epochs, defaults to 10.

  • devices (int) – Number of devices for training, defaults to 1.

  • accelerator (str) – Accelerator type (‘cpu’, ‘gpu’, ‘tpu’, ‘hpu’), defaults to ‘gpu’.

  • num_virtual_nodes (int) – Number of virtual nodes to add, defaults to 0.

  • rwse_k (int) – Random walk structural encoding steps, defaults to 0.

  • laplacian_k (int) – Laplacian positional encoding components, defaults to 0.

  • elstatic_k (int) – Electrostatic positional encoding components, defaults to 0.

  • distmat_k (int) – Distance matrix positional encoding components, defaults to 0.

  • rrwp_k (int) – Relative random walk positional encoding steps, defaults to 0.

  • feature_list (list[str] | None) – Tabular features to combine with graph features, defaults to None.

  • clip (bool) – Whether to clip predictions to the training label range, defaults to True.

  • label_encoder_params (dict) – Label encoder parameters, defaults to {}.

  • label_transform_map (str | list[str] | dict | None) – Label transform configuration, defaults to None.

  • scaler_type (str) – Type of target scaler, defaults to ‘standard’.

  • augment_resonance (bool) – Whether to augment with resonance structures, defaults to False.

  • seed (int) – Random seed, defaults to 0.

GPS (General, Powerful, Scalable) 3D graph transformer classifier for molecular conformers.

3D extension of the GPS architecture from Rampasek et al., Recipe for a General, Powerful, Scalable Graph Transformer (arXiv:2205.12454). Combines local MPNN message passing with global transformer-style attention over 3D molecular conformers. Compatible with classification datasets only.

Inherits from BaseScikitLearnGNN3D for common training and predicting routines.

References

  • https://arxiv.org/abs/2205.12454

Example usage:

model = GPS3DClassifier()
model.fit(train_mols, train_y)
predictions = model.predict(test_mols)

  • enc_readout (str) – Aggregation strategy for molecule-level embeddings, defaults to ‘vpa’.

  • enc_dropout (float) – Encoder dropout rate, defaults to 0.2.

  • enc_activation (str) – Encoder activation function, defaults to ‘gelu’.

  • pred_hidden_dims (list[int] | None) – Hidden layer dimensions in the predictor MLP, defaults to [256, 256].

  • pred_task_head_dims (list[int] | None) – Per-task head dimensions, defaults to None.

  • pred_activation (str) – Predictor activation function, defaults to ‘gelu’.

  • pred_dropout (float) – Predictor dropout rate, defaults to 0.2.

  • num_endpoints (int) – Number of endpoints or classes to predict, defaults to 1.

  • loss_fn (str) – Loss function, defaults to ‘bce’.

  • loss_args (dict) – Additional loss function arguments, defaults to {}.

  • optimizer (str) – Optimizer, defaults to ‘adamw’.

  • optimizer_args (dict) – Optimizer arguments, defaults to {‘lr’: 1e-4, ‘weight_decay’: 1e-4}.

  • scheduler (str) – Learning rate scheduler, defaults to ‘warmup_linear_decay’.

  • scheduler_args (dict) – Scheduler arguments, defaults to {‘min_lr’: 1e-5}. If ‘total_steps’ is not provided, it is auto-computed as num_epochs * ceil(len(train_data) / batch_size).

  • num_epochs (int) – Number of training epochs, defaults to 100.

  • batch_size (int) – Batch size for training and prediction, defaults to 64.

  • stochastic_weight_averaging (bool) – Whether to apply SWA after regular training, defaults to False.

  • early_stopping (bool) – Whether to enable early stopping, defaults to True.

  • patience (int) – Early stopping patience in epochs, defaults to 20.

  • devices (int) – Number of devices for training, defaults to 1.

  • accelerator (str) – Accelerator type (‘cpu’, ‘gpu’, ‘tpu’, ‘hpu’), defaults to ‘gpu’.

  • elstatic_k (int) – Electrostatic positional encoding components, defaults to 0.

  • distmat_k (int) – Distance matrix positional encoding components, defaults to 0.

  • rrwp_k (int) – Relative random walk positional encoding steps, defaults to 20.

  • num_virtual_nodes (int) – Number of virtual nodes to add, defaults to 0.

  • feature_list (list[str] | None) – Tabular features to combine with graph features, defaults to None.

  • label_encoder_params (dict) – Label encoder parameters, defaults to {}.

  • label_transform_map (str | list[str] | dict | None) – Label transform configuration, defaults to None.

  • augment_resonance (bool) – Whether to augment with resonance structures, defaults to False.

  • seed (int) – Random seed, defaults to 0.

Multi-Layer Perceptron (MLP) for molecular property classification from tabular features.

Predicts molecular properties from molecular descriptors and fingerprints. Includes deep lasso regularization and LinBnDrop linear layer stacks. Only compatible with classification datasets. Inherits from BaseScikitLearnTabular.

References:

  • Boldini et al., J. Cheminform. (2024): https://arxiv.org/abs/2311.05877

  • fast.ai LinBnDrop: https://docs.fast.ai/layers.html#linbndrop

model = MLPClassifier()
model.fit(train_mols, train_y)
predictions = model.predict(test_mols)

  • scheduler (str) – learning rate scheduler, defaults to ‘warmup_linear_decay’

  • scheduler_args (dict) – additional arguments for the scheduler, defaults to {‘min_lr’: 1e-5}. If ‘total_steps’ is not provided, it is auto-computed as num_epochs * ceil(len(train_data) / batch_size).

  • num_epochs (int) – number of epochs to train for, defaults to 100

Self-Normalizing Neural Network (SNN) for molecular property classification.

Predicts molecular properties from molecular descriptors and fingerprints. Uses SELU activations and AlphaDropout to maintain self-normalizing properties, enabling training of deep networks without batch normalization. Uses MultiLn parallel head layers for improved capacity. Only compatible with classification datasets. Inherits from BaseScikitLearnTabular.

References:

  • Klambauer et al., NeurIPS (2017): https://arxiv.org/abs/1706.02515

Example usage:

model = SNNClassifier()
model.fit(train_mols, train_y)
predictions = model.predict(test_mols)
Parameters:

  • hidden_dims (list[int]) – shape of hidden SNN layers, defaults to [256, 256]

  • num_parallel (int) – number of parallel heads in MultiLn layers, defaults to 8

  • dropout (float) – dropout rate (AlphaDropout), defaults to 0.05

  • num_endpoints (int) – number of endpoints (if multitasking) or classes (if classification) to predict, defaults to 1

  • deep_lasso_weight (float) – weight for deep lasso regularization, defaults to 0.1

  • loss_fn (str) – loss function to optimize, defaults to ‘bce’

  • loss_args (dict) – additional arguments for the loss function, defaults to {}

  • optimizer (str) – optimizer to use while training, defaults to ‘adamw’

  • optimizer_args (dict) – additional arguments for the optimizer, defaults to {‘lr’: 5e-3, ‘weight_decay’: 1e-2, ‘betas’: (0.9, 0.95)}

  • scheduler (str) – learning rate scheduler, defaults to ‘cosine_annealing_cyclic’. total_steps is auto-computed from dataset size and epochs when not explicitly provided.

  • scheduler_args (dict) – additional arguments for the scheduler, defaults to {‘min_lr’: 1e-5, ‘num_cycles’: 5}

  • num_epochs (int) – number of epochs to train for, defaults to 100

  • batch_size (int) – batch size for training and prediction, defaults to 64

  • stochastic_weight_averaging (bool) – whether to add SWA epochs after regular training, defaults to False

  • early_stopping (bool) – whether to use early stopping, defaults to True

  • patience (int) – how many epochs to wait before early stopping, defaults to 20

  • devices (int) – number of devices for training, defaults to 1

  • accelerator (str) – hardware accelerator (‘cpu’, ‘gpu’, ‘tpu’, or ‘hpu’), defaults to ‘gpu’

  • feature_list (list[str]) – descriptor/fingerprint sets to use as input, defaults to [‘ECFP_count’, ‘rdkit_all_descriptors’]

  • label_encoder_params (dict) – parameters for the label encoder, defaults to {}

  • label_transform_map (str | list[str] | dict | None) – label transform configuration, defaults to None

  • augment_resonance (bool) – whether to augment with resonance structures, defaults to False

  • seed (int) – random seed for reproducibility, defaults to 0
